# record


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A fine-tuned model is only as useful as what is known about it. Weeks
later, when a model on the Hub answers better or worse than expected,
the questions are always the same: which commit trained it, on which
data, on what machine, with which arguments, for how long. `sysone.json`
already holds what is needed to *run* a model (its template, head,
encoder and temperatures). The training record adds what is needed to
*train it again*:

</thead>

<td><code>code</code></td>
<td>the git commit, branch and remote of the repository the training ran
in, which files had uncommitted changes and a hash of the diff, and the
notebook or script that ran, with its hash</td>
</tr>

<td>Python, the operating system, the versions of the packages that
matter (torch, transformers, peft, …) and CUDA; every installed package
goes to <code>environment.txt</code> beside
<code>sysone.json</code></td>
</tr>

the host’s CPU and memory, and where the run happened: a sysone job,

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>data</code></td>
<td>where the cases came from (a Hub dataset and its commit, or a file’s
name and hash), each split’s size and fingerprint, the template,
transforms, sampler and seed</td>
</tr>

counts</td>
</tr>

defaults, every fit (epochs, learning rates, schedule, batch, precision,

The record goes to the Hub with the model, so it holds nothing private:
no absolute paths (files are named relative to their repository, or by
name), no user or host names, no tokens, and remote URLs lose any
credentials.

The fixtures: a tiny ModernBERT trained for one epoch on twenty cases.

``` python
data = TypedDecisions.from_json("fixtures/typed_decisions_tiny.jsonl", valid=0.25, calib=0.2)
learn = decision_learner(data, "fixtures/tiny-modernbert", train="lora", preset="cpu", logging_steps=1)
learn.fit_one_cycle(1, lr=1e-3);
```

## Code

[`git_info`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/record.html#git_info)
asks git about the repository holding a path: its commit, branch and
remote, and what has changed since the commit. A record is only
reproducible from a commit if nothing was changed, so the changed files
are listed (at most 50) and the whole diff is hashed: two runs with the
same commit and the same `diff_sha256` ran the same code.

href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L32"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->dict | None:
```

repository holding `path`, or None outside one*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### public_url

``` python
def public_url(
    url:str | None
)->str | None:
```

*A URL without the credentials some remotes carry
(`https://user:token@host/...`)*

``` python
g = git_info()
{k: g[k] for k in ("repo", "branch", "dirty", "n_changed")}
```

``` python
test_eq(len(g["commit"]), 40)
test_eq(git_info(tempfile.mkdtemp()), None)
test_eq(public_url("https://me:hf_secret@github.com/me/repo.git"), "https://github.com/me/repo.git")
test_eq(public_url("git@github.com:me/repo.git"), "git@github.com:me/repo.git")
```

[`entry_point`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/record.html#entry_point)
names what is running. A sysone job says so in `SYSONE_ENTRY`; Jupyter
puts a notebook’s path in `JPY_SESSION_NAME` (or `__session__`), VS Code
in `__vsc_ipynb_file__`; a script is `sys.argv[0]`. The name is relative
to the file’s repository, and the file’s hash tells whether it changed
since.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L52"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### entry_point

``` python
def entry_point()->dict | None:
```

*The notebook or script that is running: its name, relative to its git
repository, and its SHA-256*

``` python
nb = Path("05a_record.ipynb").resolve()
os.environ["SYSONE_ENTRY"] = str(nb)
test_eq(entry_point()["name"], "nbs/05a_record.ipynb")
os.environ["SYSONE_ENTRY"] = "/somewhere/else/train.py"
test_eq(entry_point(), {"name": "train.py"})
del os.environ["SYSONE_ENTRY"]
```

[`hardware`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/cloud.html#hardware)
describes the accelerator a run trains on, the host around it, and where
the run happens. A job started by `sysone.cloud` names its backend and
id in `SYSONE_JOB`; otherwise Colab, Kaggle and SageMaker each leave a
variable of their own in the environment, and anything else is a local
run.

## Data

[`data_record`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/record.html#data_record)
reads what the loaders noted in `TypedDecisions.source`, and adds each
split’s size and fingerprint. A fingerprint is `datasets`’ hash of a
split’s content and of the transformations that made it, so the same
cases split the same way get the same fingerprints. For a Hub dataset,
the record also asks the Hub which commit the revision points to (unless
the Hub is offline), so a dataset that changes later can still be loaded
as it was: `TypedDecisions.from_hub(id, revision=sha)`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L149"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->dict:
```

*Where a
[`TypedDecisions`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/data.html#typeddecisions)’
cases came from, each split’s size and fingerprint, its template,
transforms, sampler and seed*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L140"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### hub_sha

``` python
def hub_sha(
    repo:str, revision:str | None=None, repo_type:str='dataset'
)->str | None:
```

*The commit a Hub repo’s revision points to, or None offline or on any
error*

``` python
dr = data_record(learn.data)
test_eq({k: v["cases"] for k, v in dr["splits"].items()}, {k: len(v) for k, v in learn.data.cases.items() if v is not None})
test_eq(data_record(TypedDecisions.from_json("fixtures/typed_decisions_tiny.jsonl", valid=0.25, calib=0.2))["splits"], dr["splits"])
dr
```

## The record

The training part keeps the arguments that differ from transformers’
defaults, not all of `TrainingArguments` (more than a hundred fields),
and leaves out paths and tokens. The learner’s
[`FitLog`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/learner.html#fitlog)
callback gives one entry per fit, and the loss history is thinned to at
most 500 points.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L190"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### thin

``` python
def thin(
    xs:list, n:int=500
)->list:
```

*At most `n` evenly spaced items of `xs`, the first and the last among
them*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/models.py#L601"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


### jsonable

``` python
def jsonable(
    v
):
```

*A value as JSON can hold it: enums by value, containers element by
element, anything else by `str`*

``` python
args = non_default_args(learn.args)
test_eq((args["lr_scheduler_type"], args["remove_unused_columns"]), ("cosine", False))
assert not any("dir" in k or "token" in k for k in args)
test_eq(lora_config(learn.model)["peft_type"], "LORA")
test_eq(thin(list(range(10)), 4), [0, 3, 6, 9])
test_eq(jsonable({"a": {2, 1}, "b": transformers.trainer_utils.SchedulerType.COSINE}), {"a": [1, 2], "b": "cosine"})
```

[`tracking_info`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/record.html#tracking_info)
notes the MLflow run a training logged to: the one a tracking callback
kept on the learner (`learn.tracking`), else the run active in this
process. A tracking URI is shortened the same way as a git remote: a
local store becomes its kind, a server its address without credentials.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L203"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tracking_info

``` python
def tracking_info(
    learn:NoneType=None
)->dict | None:
```

*The MLflow run that logged a training: what a tracking callback kept on
the learner, else the active run, else None*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L196"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### public_tracking_uri

``` python
def public_tracking_uri(
    uri:str | None
)->str | None:
```

*A tracking URI without local paths or credentials: `file` or `sqlite`
for local stores, the address of a server, an ARN as it is*

``` python
test_eq([public_tracking_uri(u) for u in ("file:///Users/me/mlruns", "sqlite:///mlflow.db", "http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:5000",
         "arn:aws:sagemaker:us-east-1:123456789012:mlflow-app/app-1")],
        ["file", "sqlite", "http://127.0.0.1:5000", "arn:aws:sagemaker:us-east-1:123456789012:mlflow-app/app-1"])
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/record.py#L215"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### training_record

``` python
def training_record(
    learn
)->dict:
```

*What trained a learner’s model, and how to train it again: code,
environment, hardware, data, model, fits, tracking, and what it
continued*

``` python
rec = training_record(learn)
text = json.dumps(rec)
for private in (str(Path.home()), str(Path.cwd()), platform.node()):
    assert not private or private not in text, f"the record leaks {private!r}"
test_eq((rec["model"]["regime"], rec["training"]["preset"], len(rec["training"]["fits"])), ("lora", "cpu", 1))
test_eq(rec["data"]["source"]["kind"], "file")
{k: rec[k] for k in ("model", "training")} | {"training": {k: rec["training"][k] for k in ("preset", "loss", "lr", "seed", "fits")}}
```

``` python
learn.resumed_from = {"name": "first", "source": "first", "training": {"recorded": "2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}    # as load_learner leaves it
test_eq(training_record(learn)["resumed_from"]["name"], "first")
del learn.resumed_from
```

A job runs in a folder of its own, away from any repository, on a
machine that may have no git at all. So [remote](40_cloud.ipynb) records
the git state of the checkout it was started from, the job hands it on
as `SYSONE_SOURCE`, and the record falls back on it:

``` python
os.environ["SYSONE_SOURCE"] = json.dumps({"git": {"repo": "project", "commit": "0123abc", "dirty": False}, "sysone_git": None})
with working_directory(tempfile.mkdtemp()): code = training_record(learn)["code"]
test_eq(code["git"]["commit"], "0123abc")
del os.environ["SYSONE_SOURCE"]
```

`learn.export` writes the record into `sysone.json` under `training`,
and the package list into `environment.txt` (see
[inference](06_inference.ipynb#export)); the model card on the Hub is
written from both (see [hub](42_hub.ipynb)).
